uno-q.description: Arduino UNO Q — dual-brain STM32U585 MCU + QRB2210 MPU (Linux with App Lab containers)
uno-q.agent_cli_install_hint: App Lab `brick compose` is the native container manager. Prefer `brick compose exec python <cmd>` over plain docker.

safety_assertions.firmware_mcu_bin_flash_command_hint: MCU sketch via `arduino-cli compile --fqbn arduino:mbed_nano:stm32u585xx` → deploy via `brick flash` or App Lab UI.

m5core2-esp32.description: M5Stack Core2 ESP32 (ARMIC wearable, 6-topic MQTT publisher)
m5core2-esp32.os: FreeRTOS / ESP-IDF (flashed via Arduino IDE, not SSH)
notes: This profile is metadata-only. The M5 Core2 itself does not accept SSH — its MQTT broker lives on the UNO Q MPU python container at port 1883.
Use the `uno-q` host alias and run mosquitto_pub/_sub on the MPU python container to test the wearable envelope instead.

generic-linux-arduino-host.description: Catch-all for any SSH-reachable Linux board (Raspberry Pi, Orange Pi, other SBC) running an Arduino-compatible toolchain or hosting a USB-connected Arduino.
notes: If you have an Arduino board attached via USB serial to this host, install arduino-cli via board_setup then use `arduino-cli compile` / `arduino-cli upload` over ssh_exec.
